forces.title: Rising operating costs erode retail profit margins.
forces.description: Dutch retailers, including supermarkets, face increasing pressure on profit margins from rising sourcing, logistics, and labor costs. Despite sales growth, intense price competition and cautious, price-sensitive consumers limit the ability to fully pass these higher costs onto customers. This creates a significant challenge for translating top-line revenue growth into bottom-line profitability, leading to sustained margin erosion across food, non-food, and e-commerce segments.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: E-commerce steadily expands market share, challenging traditional retail.
forces.description: E-commerce continues its long-term shift towards online shopping in the Netherlands, steadily increasing its share of total retail sales and strengthening its position at the expense of traditional channels. This structural change necessitates ongoing investment in digital capabilities by physical retailers. While the era of double-digit growth is over, sustained robust growth in online sales mandates that grocery and hypermarket operators continue to adapt their business models to effectively compete in a hybrid retail landscape.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: Multichannel retailers regain online market share, leveraging physical networks.
forces.description: In a significant shift, multichannel retailers in the Netherlands have begun to outperform online-only retailers in online sales growth for the first time since 2022. This trend, particularly strong in segments like supermarkets, indicates that traditional retailers' investments in digital capabilities, such as websites, mobile apps, and logistics, are paying off. Their extensive physical store networks, offering click-and-collect and local fulfillment, provide a competitive advantage by combining online convenience with in-store engagement.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: AI redefines store value beyond traditional four-wall P&L.
forces.description: Retailers must now manage physical stores as a portfolio of nodes, recognizing their value extends far beyond direct sales and traditional four-wall profit and loss. AI-driven insights enable real-time measurement of broader contributions, such as anchoring click-and-collect traffic, enhancing brand awareness, enabling retail media revenue, and serving as inventory buffers. This strategic shift requires redefining KPIs and investment decisions to reflect a store's overall ecosystem value and resilience, ensuring optimal capital allocation across the network.
forces.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

forces.title: AI integration revolutionizes retail operations, enhancing efficiency and decision-making.
forces.description: AI is becoming embedded throughout retail operations, transforming frontline workflows by powering real-time decisions on pricing, labor, and inventory replenishment. The integration of AI into in-store technologies like digital shelf labels, RFID, computer vision, and POS systems significantly improves data tracking and trend responsiveness. This widespread adoption of AI not only streamlines store operations and order fulfillment but also provides a foundation for more agile, data-based, and continuously optimized actions, driving substantial operational efficiency gains for grocery and hypermarket retailers.
forces.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

forces.title: Omnichannel innovation positions physical stores as fulfillment and digital hubs.
forces.description: Leading retailers are increasingly leveraging physical stores as strategic infrastructure to support broader omnichannel ecosystems. Examples like Walmart and Alibaba's Freshippo demonstrate how stores function not just as retail floors but also as efficient fulfillment hubs for online orders and digital engagement nodes. This model drives superior sales per unit area and allows for rapid local delivery, creating cost-to-serve advantages and enhancing customer convenience. This structural shift transforms stores into multi-functional assets essential for modern retail success.
forces.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

forces.title: Increased operating costs and talent shortages pressure Irish grocery margins.
forces.description: Irish grocery retailers face significant headwinds from increased operating costs, including rising minimum wages, pension auto-enrolment, and insurance expenses. Compounding this, an acute shortage of personnel in a 'full employment' environment makes recruitment and retention challenging. These factors contribute to elevated overheads, forcing retailers to intensely focus on margin development and preservation in a highly competitive market, while also addressing a dwindling talent pipeline for future store ownership.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Strong own-brand offerings crucial for customer engagement and margin growth.
forces.description: In Ireland, as consumers prioritize saving money on food, a strong own-brand offering has become critical for leading grocery brands to maintain customer engagement and improve margins. Retailers are responding with increased promotion, prominence, and discernible improvements in their own-brand range, including premium, healthy, and sustainable options. This strategy is essential for meeting evolving customer expectations and preserving profitability in an inflationary market, providing a distinct competitive advantage.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Digital transformation and automation essential for Irish grocery profitability.
forces.description: The Irish grocery sector's fragmented digital transformation has led to operational inefficiencies and delays in optimizing supply chains, analytics, and omnichannel models. Recognizing this, retailers are prioritizing investment in digital initiatives to preserve profitability, including electronic shelf labels, self-scan checkouts, smart rostering, robots, and IoT. These technologies facilitate dynamic pricing, reduced out-of-stock situations, efficient re-ordering, and improved promotions, all crucial for sustaining margins in a high-volume, low-margin environment while meeting consumer expectations.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Growing 'silver economy' presents significant opportunity for Irish retailers.
forces.description: Ireland's population aged over 65 has doubled in twenty years to 800,000, projected to reach 1.5 million by 2050, aligning with the European 'silver economy' expected to represent over 35% of spending consumption by 2030. This demographic shift presents a significant tailwind for Irish retailers, including grocery and hypermarket operators, who must strategically adapt their product offerings, store layouts, and services to meet the evolving needs and preferences of this rapidly growing and economically influential consumer segment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: AI reshaping customer discovery and engagement across retail.
forces.description: AI is fundamentally altering how customers discover, compare, and navigate products, even in traditional retail sectors. AI-mediated discovery and AI assistants are becoming key touchpoints, recommending brands and shaping purchase decisions. This structural change necessitates that grocery, hypermarket, and value retailers invest heavily in content and data infrastructure to boost visibility in AI-driven environments. Ensuring brand content and product information is intelligible to AI systems is crucial for maintaining relevance and customer engagement in this evolving digital landscape.
forces.source_title: The State of Luxury: What US and Chinese clients reveal about the sector’s future

forces.title: Generative AI transforms retailer demand value chain capabilities.
forces.description: Generative AI and agentic models are expanding AI's impact across the entire demand value chain for retailers, moving beyond traditional analytics. These technologies enable retailers to process unstructured consumer signals, create and test concepts faster, and orchestrate actions within guardrails. Retailers are deploying AI for critical functions such as pricing, assortment optimization, demand forecasting, inventory management, store operations, and personalized marketing, signifying a profound structural shift in how retailers achieve efficiency and engagement, including grocery and hypermarket operators.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

forces.title: Lack of AI ROI measurement hinders full-scale retail transformation.
forces.description: Over half of retailers do not formally measure the ROI of their consumer AI investments, posing a significant risk to successful, sustainable transformation. A common barrier to scaling is that pilot economics often fail to translate into full-scale ROI due to complexities like live data, legacy systems, and cross-functional tradeoffs. This measurement gap prevents clear business case validation and makes it difficult for retailers, including grocery chains, to justify and scale promising AI initiatives, potentially leading to missed growth and productivity opportunities.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

forces.title: Shifting AI from 'copilot' to 'autopilot' for massive efficiency gains.
forces.description: The evolution of AI from a 'copilot' that generates insights for human decision-makers to an 'autopilot' that executes decisions within guardrails represents a profound upside driver for retail. Processes like demand forecasting can transition to continuous AI execution, automatically refreshing forecasts and triggering allocation/replenishment actions with human oversight for exceptions. This shift, while requiring robust governance and clear guardrails, promises significant efficiency gains, reduced human intervention in routine tasks, and faster, more agile responses to market dynamics for grocery and hypermarket operators.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

forces.title: AI adoption reshapes retail functions and operating models.
forces.description: The effective implementation of AI in retail necessitates a fundamental reshaping of demand value chain functions and operating models. Work becomes more cross-functional, requiring enhanced collaboration across marketing, sales, merchandising, supply chain, data, and technology teams. Roles shift towards orchestration, oversight, relationship management, and strategic trade-off decisions. For instance, the merchandising role is evolving, with AI handling analytical and operational tasks, allowing merchants to focus on category strategy, supplier relationships, and commercial judgment, signifying a deep structural change for grocery and hypermarket organizations.
forces.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead

viewpoints.title: Dutch retail profitability faces growing pressure despite sales growth.
viewpoints.description: ING Think anticipates Dutch retail sales growth of 3% in 2026, driven by a 4.5% increase in e-commerce, with supermarkets gaining online market share. However, escalating sourcing, logistics, and labor costs, combined with fierce price competition and cautious consumer spending, are intensely squeezing profit margins. This challenging environment makes it increasingly difficult for retailers to translate revenue growth into higher profits, indicating a sustained period of profitability pressure for the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

viewpoints.title: Irish retail sector faces volume decline and uneven consumer spending challenges.
viewpoints.description: Allianz_ie notes Irish retail sales volumes declined by 0.2% month-on-month and 0.5% year-on-year in April 2026, reflecting weak real growth. While sales value rose, consumer spending is uneven due to persistent cost-of-living pressures. Subsectors like clothing, department stores, and electrical goods saw significant declines. Rising energy costs, high rents, and labor shortages intensify profitability pressures, with increasing insolvencies indicating a challenging environment for many retailers, including those in grocery.

viewpoints.title: Leading Irish grocery brands show robust health and positive market outlook.
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland observes significant new store openings and extensive revamps across the Irish grocery, convenience, and forecourt markets in 2026, reflecting the competitive yet robust financial health of leading brands. Despite increased operating costs, regulatory burdens, and elevated grocery inflation (c4% in June/July 2026), strong take-home grocery sales persist. Retailers are strategically focusing on margin development and expanding own-brand offerings to sustain customer engagement and address cost-conscious consumers, indicating a cautiously positive, adaptive market.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: Although consumers remain cautious, improved purchasing power is providing underlying support for spending in the Dutch retail sector.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Research forecasts Dutch retail sales to increase by 3% in 2026, matching the previous year's growth. E-commerce is expected to be the primary driver.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

demand_drivers.description: Despite the end of double-digit growth, the fundamental consumer preference shift towards online purchasing continues to drive e-commerce expansion, increasing its share of total retail sales.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Research forecasts e-commerce turnover growth for the Netherlands. This is a specific growth rate for the online retail channel.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

demand_drivers.description: Food retail benefits from being a less discretionary spending category, allowing it to maintain steady growth even with cautious consumer behavior and improved purchasing power.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Research provides a forecast growth rate for the food retail segment in the Netherlands.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

demand_drivers.description: While purchasing power improves, overall consumer caution limits growth in non-food segments, leading to more modest increases compared to e-commerce or food retail.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Research provides a forecast growth rate for the non-food retail segment in the Netherlands.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

pnl_drivers.description: Lower consumer goods price increases (1.5% in 1H26 vs 2.4% in 1H25) indicate moderated inflation and potentially reduced ability for retailers to pass on rising operational costs to consumers, pressuring margins.

market_sizing.methodology: Consumer Price Index (CPI) data from CBS, analyzed by ING Research, indicates the average increase in consumer goods prices for the first seven months of 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

pnl_drivers.description: Food inflation eased significantly to less than 1% between January and July 2026 from 4% in 2025. This reduces pricing power for food retailers, exerting pressure on their profit margins unless cost efficiencies are achieved.

market_sizing.methodology: CBS data, analyzed by ING Research, shows the year-on-year price increase for food and non-alcoholic beverages during the specified period.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

pnl_drivers.description: Declining retail sales volumes (0.5% YoY) reflect weakened real growth, driven by ongoing cost-of-living pressures which curb discretionary spending and impact overall purchasing decisions in the Irish market.

market_sizing.methodology: Allianz_ie reports the month-on-month and year-on-year change in Irish retail sales volumes for April 2026, based on official data.

pnl_drivers.description: The 1.0% increase in retail sales value year-on-year in April 2026 masks underlying weak-to-flat real growth. This suggests that price increases, rather than increased purchasing volume, are contributing to value growth, which may still pressure retailer profitability and consumer affordability.

market_sizing.methodology: Allianz_ie reports the year-on-year change in the value of Irish retail sales for April 2026.

pnl_drivers.description: Irish grocery inflation remained elevated at approximately 4% in June/July 2026. This reflects higher global commodity prices (wheat, sugar, cocoa), increased overheads for retailers and suppliers, rising farm gate prices, and global trade uncertainty, all contributing to margin pressures for grocery operators.

market_sizing.methodology: Bank of Ireland reports the level of Irish grocery inflation in June/July 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

pnl_drivers.description: Scaling a full set of relevant AI initiatives across the demand value chain can deliver 180 to 360 basis points of cumulative EBIT for retailers. This indicates a significant opportunity for margin improvement and profitability enhancement through technological adoption and operational transformation.

market_sizing.methodology: BCG's experience with clients in scaling individual AI initiatives across the demand value chain. This represents potential EBIT increase, not a market size.
market_sizing.source_title: AI in CPG and Retail: How Winners Are Pulling Ahead
